title: Make a daily briefing in Claude (desktop app)
description: The same lesson as the CLI take, phrased for the Claude desktop app: build a reusable daily-briefing prompt, run it, then have Claude set it up to arrive automatically each weekday morning.
comment: First authoring run on the real app should confirm the exact wording of step 3 against the app's current scheduled-tasks UI, then freeze markers from what actually appears on screen — same calibrate-once flow as the CLI recipe.

steps.narration: Open the Claude app. This is a real Claude session — everything you're about to see is live.

steps.input: I want a daily morning briefing. Here is my day: 09:30 policy team stand-up; 11:00 1:1 with my director about the AI skills programme; 14:00 digital inclusion working group; a procurement briefing note due today; and an urgent inbox flag that the note's deadline moved to 15:00. Give me a punchy one-minute briefing: today's meetings, top 3 priorities, anything urgent — under 150 words.
steps.narration: Step 1 — Paste your day and ask for a one-minute briefing: meetings, top 3 priorities, anything urgent.

steps.input: Turn that into a reusable prompt I can run every morning with fresh calendar and inbox details, and keep the same three-section format.
steps.narration: Step 2 — Ask Claude to turn it into a reusable morning-briefing prompt you can run every day.

steps.input: Set this up so it runs automatically every weekday at 9am and the briefing is waiting for me when I open Claude.
steps.narration: Step 3 — Ask Claude to schedule it: every weekday at 9am, the briefing is waiting for you.
That's it — a daily morning briefing in the Claude app, set up in one short conversation.
